newsitem.title: FRANCE: Western-powered Russian jumbo set for Dec take off.
newsitem.headline: Western-powered Russian jumbo set for Dec take off.

text.p: Ilyushin said Russian certification of its wide-bodied IL-96T -- the country's first western-powered long-haul cargo jet -- is on schedule to allow it to enter service with Aeroflot in December.
Ilyushin first deputy general designer Viacheslav Terentyev told Reuters in an interview that certification of both the passenger and cargo types of the plane should be completed by mid-1998.

He said certification schedules of both the U.S. and Russia have been running in parallel, with officials from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) witnessing all tests undertaken at the main Ilyushin aviation complex at Voronezh, 550 km south of Moscow.
Upon completion, Terentyev said, they would sign a bilateral agreement recognising each other's flight certification procedures and standards.

"More than 70 meetings have been held between Russian and U.S. FAA officials to clarify the certification process for airborne systems, avionics, power plans, airframe, materials, after-sales support and flight test procedures," he said.
He conceded that a few engineering issues remained, including flight-stall indicator acceptance and the IL-96's landing gear.
This has required additional FAA tests, said Terentyev.

Ilyushin design bureau spokesman Alexander Shakhnovitch told Reuters in Moscow that the IL-96T cargo aircraft offers 776 cubic metres of cargo space, of which 580 metres are on the upper deck, where larger cargo pieces can be accommodated.
He added this plane could carry 92 tonnes up to 5,200 km and 30 tonnes up to 14,000 km.
The IL-96M will be able to carry up to 436 passengers with a total payload of 58 tonnes. Its bellyhold cargo carrying capacity is unspecified.
The IL-96T freighter has a wide cargo loading door, 2.875 metres high and 4.850 metres wide.

Ilyushin interrupted continuing Russian and U.S. certification programmes last week to allow the first production IL-96T cargo plane to make its maiden appearance outside Russia at the Paris Air Show.

Powered by four U.S. Pratt & Whitney PW-2337 engines, this version is due for delivery to Aeroflot Russian International Airlines at the end of this year and will be operated on routes from Moscow to Singapore, Tokyo, Dubai and Novostock, said Terentyev.
Certification of the IL-96M passenger version will follow, he added, and will only recover additional approval for interior materials, including rescue, evacuation and emergency equipment.

In addition to firm orders for three IL-96Ts and 17 IL-96Ms from Aeroflot, Terentyev said Ilyushin hoped that after FAA certification it would win sales outside the former Soviet Union from leasing firms, cargo and charter operators and emerging market airlines.
